tagline: Degrading benzophenone-3 before it reaches our waters
summary: ABOA (University of Turku) set out to express the benzophenone-3 (BP-3, oxybenzone) catabolic pathway of Rhodococcus oxybenzonivorans in E. coli so that this sunscreen UV filter could be destroyed inside a wastewater treatment plant rather than released into the Baltic and the oceans. The team built a modular restriction-based plasmid system (10 plasmids, 10 genes covering four pathway steps, codon-optimised and RFC10/RFC1000 compatible) that lets homologous flavin reductases and flavin-dependent oxidoreductases be co-expressed, separated, swapped and re-tagged between 6xHis and GST using only NcoI, NdeI and XhoI. Enzyme expression and solubility were obtained to varying degrees, but the activity question was not resolved: BP-3 and BP-1 absorbance overlaps NADH so the spectrophotometric assay was inconclusive, and the triple-quadrupole LC-MS run failed on missing controls and incompatible vials. The team says this plainly and positions the work as a first step plus a designed-but-untested 28-part Golden Gate system (38 parts in total) handed to the community.

dry.frameworks: No modelling framework. The /model, /software and /hardware pages are unfilled iGEM template stubs carrying only the award description text, which is worth stating plainly: this project has essentially no dry-lab component.
dry.dataviz: Hand-drawn schematic figures only: the proposed R. oxybenzonivorans catabolic pathway, the plasmid map set, the LC-MS detection strategy, the Golden Gate assembly map, and a single process diagram running from the Golden Gate construct to a fixed-carrier bioreactor at the end of a wastewater plant. Survey results are reported as percentages in prose rather than plotted.
dry.datascience: A 136-response consumer survey on sunscreen habits and environmental awareness (93% use sunscreen regularly; 68% say environmental friendliness influences purchase; 57% aware some sunscreen ingredients harm the environment; 52% read ingredient lists; 52% believe sunscreen slows tanning but only 9% skip it for that reason; 70% would protect their skin over the environment if forced to choose). Percentages are honestly computed per question because response counts varied. No statistical modelling.
dry.software: None. Sequence work was done with off-the-shelf tools: NCBI protein BLAST to find Rhodococcus homologues of every proposed pathway enzyme, Benchling for the Golden Gate overhang design and SnapGene for visualising the final construct.
techniques: homologue search across Rhodococcus strains (USK10, USK13, R. jostii, R. oxybenzonivorans)
Golden Gate overhang design (BsaI, six positions A-F in pET28g)

good.publicEngagement: A 136-person anonymous survey on sunscreen habits collected at public events and on social media, designed both to gather data and to raise awareness; it was later used to shape the team's social posts. Secondary-school visits with age-split formats (project pitch plus a Kahoot on synthetic biology fundamentals for upper secondary; a hands-on osmosis experiment for lower secondary), with a return invitation and a further school event booked for after the Jamboree. A red-cabbage pH indicator workshop for primary-school children at Turku main library during Turku Day, linked out to ocean acidification. A joint appearance with Aalto-Helsinki at Children's Medical Day at the Heureka Science Centre (22 August 2026) running three workshops, where the team also collected survey responses. An article about the project and about iGEM in the magazine of Suomen Solubiologit ry (the Finnish cell biologists' association), with a follow-up article agreed for after the Jamboree. A laboratory visit by science journalist Ritva Setala and photographer Marttiina Sairanen from the regional newspaper Turun Sanomat. Recruitment-oriented booths at the Study in Turku fair and the TYY Opening Carnival with Aboa Turku ry, where the team deliberately worked against first-year students' sense that an international synthetic biology competition is beyond them.
good.ihp: ABOA's integrated human practices is genuinely integrated on the technical side and well-documented in method: previous ABOA teams advised contacting stakeholders before the project idea was fixed, and the team set a rule that every meeting had a written objective beforehand and a debrief afterwards whose notes fed project decisions. The strongest single causal chain runs through the Turku wastewater treatment plant. Process engineer Jouko Tuomi, with trainees Nea Lempiainen and Heli Karinkanta, told them that purified enzymes are too delicate and expensive to run in a plant, that enzyme activity decays, and that whole cells on fixed carriers in a flow-through bioreactor are what the activated sludge process already does well - and the team changed its implementation from purified enzymes to intact cells as a result, then built a Golden Gate system specifically to put all pathway enzymes into one cell. The same conversation produced three further changes: they dropped the idea of inoculating their strain into the activated sludge itself because the plant warned it would wreck the existing microbial balance for months and their strain would simply be out-competed; they moved the bioreactor to the end of the treatment train after filtration, with coagulation and UV kill as the existing backstop; and they took up the plant's suggestion of treating a concentrated side stream rather than the whole flow, since influent BP-3 is too dilute to treat economically. The plant also told them that in Finland plants operate underground so mining new space costs tens of millions of euros and changes are made essentially only when law requires them, and that efficiency ranks above cost in technology selection - which is why the team's own staging plan is wastewater-sample testing, then a small on-site test station, then integration. A second chain runs through the construct design: Dr. Rongbin Wang's explanation that BioBrick parts cannot cleanly build in-frame fusion proteins or swap purification tags made the team abandon the BioBrick route entirely for expression-ready plasmids modified with standard restriction enzymes; Dr. Jarmo Kapyla's point that neither His- nor GST-tag performance can be predicted made them commit to testing both experimentally with His as primary and GST as backup, and also told them colony PCR is insufficient verification (they could not afford sequencing primers and say so, recommending sequencing for the next stage); Dr. Tuomas Huovinen supplied concrete expression parameters they adopted (200 mL culture to OD600 0.8, 0.4 mM IPTG, 26 C post-induction, 16 h), the Western blot with HRP-conjugated anti-6xHis antibodies to see proteins SDS-PAGE could not, and electroporation to fix poor heat-shock transformation. A third chain is about not making the problem worse: Dr. Timo Vuorisalo (ecology) told them to check whether the pathway intermediates might themselves be endocrine disruptors, so they searched the ECHA ED Expert Group assessment list and found none of the intermediates listed; Professor Tuulia Hyotylainen (exposomes, Orebro) confirmed that degrading one aromatic ring is very likely to abolish the endocrine activity, which validated attacking only the early pathway steps, and warned that wastewater conditions will be far less favourable than the lab bench; Professor Emma Camp (Future Reefs, UTS) added that the bacteria must be tested under realistic wastewater conditions and contained, and that BP-3 is one stressor among many on reefs rather than the main one. Harri Helminen of the Finnish supervisory agency confirmed UV filters are among the top five endocrine disruptors of concern in water ecosystems, told them no comprehensive BP-3 measurement exists for Finnish waters, explained that Environmental Quality Standards are set 100-1000 times below the lowest concentration with observed biological effect, and placed BP-3 within the revised EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive (in force 2025, requirements generally expected by 2036, 80% micropollutant removal) - which is the regulatory anchor for the whole project. Health-side consultations changed emphasis rather than engineering: Merike Laine of the Helsinki Allergy and Asthma Association said UV filters are less prominent allergens than fragrances and preservatives, so the team deliberately de-emphasised skin reactions, and dermatologist Dr. Susanna Majasuo prompted them to research why BP-3 is already regulated and to add a comparison of alternative UV filters, which they did, and to run the consumer survey. Cosmetic manufacturer Dermosil explained that the industry has moved from single filters to multi-filter formulations (naming Diethylamino Hydroxybenzoyl Hexyl Benzoate, Ethylhexyl Triazone, Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine and others) and that approved filters' risks are outweighed by unprotected UV exposure - useful context, though it mainly validated rather than redirected the project. Where this IHP is weaker than its documentation suggests is that the central technical claim was never demonstrated: no stakeholder input could rescue the activity assay, and the Golden Gate system the WWTP conversation motivated remains untested in the lab.
good.realWorld: Implementation is specified concretely and in the plant's own terms: an enclosed bioreactor placed as a biological post-treatment step after the activated sludge process and a filtration step, with engineered E. coli immobilised on cellulose via an adhesive catecholamine moiety or on polystyrene beads to make coated filters, followed by coagulation and UV inactivation of escapees, plus a kill switch for environments outside the reactor and engineered auxotrophy as a further containment layer. The driver is regulatory and dated: the revised EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive entered force in 2025 and requires 80% removal of micropollutants including BP-3, with requirements generally expected to be met by 2036, and the team notes that ozonation leaves incompletely degraded residues, activated carbon only adsorbs and is expensive to replace, and reverse osmosis/nanofiltration achieved 95% BP removal in a South Korean pilot but at high capital and energy cost. SDG claims name sub-targets - 6.3, 14.1, 14.2, 14.7, 2.1, 12.4, 12.8, 11.4, 11.5, 11.6, 8.4, 8.9, 1.4, 13.3 - and are backed by cited literature on coral ecosystem services and BP concentrations (influent up to 3795 ug/L and effluent 223 ug/L in the UK; up to 241 ng/g dry weight in Hawaiian coral tissue; zooxanthellae harmed at chronic exposure as low as 60 ng/L). The outstanding feature is the Limitations and conflicts section, which is more honest than most: it states that implementation cost could not be estimated because it is highly regional and that even Finnish industry professionals could not help, that Finnish wastewater temperatures differ from the most BP-3-affected regions so strain survival and efficiency may not transfer, that high cost could worsen inequality between developed and developing countries, that the team cannot guarantee the degradation intermediates are safe to release, that the SDG 2030 horizon is unreachable for a technology needing years more development, that a plant-based solution may be less effective than one deployed at beaches, and that the project could be used for greenwashing of reef tourism - concluding that the best solution is to limit BP-3 use altogether and that Benzophe-none is explicitly the second-best option. After the Jamboree: 38 registry parts (10 characterised expression parts plus the 28-part untested Golden Gate set), a follow-up Suomen Solubiologit article, a school event already booked, and a continuing recruitment pipeline through Aboa Turku ry for the 2027 team.

gemsTakeaway: Take ABOA's two transferable habits: write the objective of every stakeholder meeting before it happens and debrief it into notes immediately afterwards so the decision trail survives, and write an explicit Limitations and conflicts section that names the SDG trade-offs your own project creates - cost-driven inequity, unknown intermediate toxicity, and the risk of being used for greenwashing - rather than only the goals it serves.
